Revid vs VEXI: Auto-Mode Video or Your Whole Social Media?
Revid makes short-form videos and its Auto-Mode publishes them on its own. VEXI edits your own footage, designs posts and carousels, and posts it all.
Revid makes and publishes short-form video on autopilot. Here is how it compares with one app that runs your business's whole feed.

Revid turns a prompt, a script, a link, audio or a PDF into short-form videos. Its Auto-Mode keeps a content plan moving: it writes the script, makes the video and publishes it to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and X. Growth is $39 a month ($32 billed yearly) with 3 Auto-Mode workers; Ultra is $199 a month with 10.

VEXI (formerly Social Realtr) is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.

Credit where it is due: Revid already publishes on its own, today. The difference is what goes out. Revid makes videos from prompts and links, mostly for growing channels. VEXI makes your feed: your own clips edited with B-roll, music and captions, designed posts and carousels, captions and long-form video, all from one conversation about your business. VEXI costs more than Revid: plans are $199, $399 or $599 a month. What you pay for is the work you no longer do.
Revid builds videos from prompts, scripts and links. Its pages do not describe editing the clips you filmed.
Send VEXI the clips you shot and they come back cut, with B-roll, music and captions, sized for each platform.
Its pages describe no designed posts or carousels. Only video goes out.
VEXI designs the post with your logo, colors, fonts and voice. Tap anything on the design to change it.
Auto-Mode runs through workers you configure, one per stream of content.
In VEXI it is one conversation: posts, videos, designs and captions, made in your logo, colors, fonts and the way you write.
Revid is rated 3.9 on Trustpilot. Some reviewers report bugs, ignored prompts, credits used faster than expected and support that is hard to reach.
